content.overview: Section 378ZO provides for conciliation or arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 for specified disputes relating to the formation, management or business of a Producer Company between the listed categories of Members, former Members, persons claiming membership, nominees, the company, its Board, office-bearers, liquidator and specified directors or representatives. The Explanation includes specified debt, surety and produce-supply claims. A question whether a dispute relates to formation, management or business is referred to the arbitrator, whose decision is final.
content.glance: Specified Producer Company formation, management or business disputes between the listed parties are settled by conciliation or arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZO (Disputes). For disputes relating to the formation, management or business of a Producer Company between the categories of parties listed in subsection (1), the section provides for conciliation or arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, treating the parties as if they had consented in writing. The Explanation includes claims for debts or other amounts due; specified surety claims following recovery by the Producer Company from the surety; claims by the Producer Company against a Member for failure to supply required produce; and claims by a Member against the Producer Company for not taking goods supplied. Under subsection (2), a question whether the dispute relates to formation, management or business is referred to the arbitrator, whose decision is final. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Covered disputes and parties
sections.body: Subsection (1) covers disputes relating to formation, management or business of a Producer Company among Members, former Members, persons claiming to be Members or nominees of deceased Members; between such persons and the Producer Company, its Board, office-bearers or past/present liquidator; and between the Producer Company or its Board and directors, office-bearers, former directors or specified nominees, heirs or legal representatives of deceased directors.

sections.heading: Conciliation or arbitration
sections.body: The covered disputes are settled by conciliation or arbitration as provided under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, as if the parties had consented in writing to determination by conciliation or arbitration.

sections.heading: Included claim types
sections.body: The Explanation includes claims for debts or other amounts due; specified claims by a surety against the principal debtor after the Producer Company has recovered from the surety because of the principal debtor's default; claims by the Producer Company against a Member for failure to supply produce as required; and claims by a Member against the Producer Company for not taking goods supplied.

sections.heading: Question about subject-matter
sections.body: If a question arises whether a dispute relates to formation, management or business of the Producer Company, subsection (2) refers that question to the arbitrator, whose decision on it is final.

examples.title: Member supply dispute
examples.body: A claim by the Producer Company against a Member for failure to supply produce as required, or a claim by a Member that the Producer Company did not take goods supplied, falls within the categories expressly included in the section's Explanation, subject to the provision's scope and facts.

hypotheticals.question: A Member disputes the Producer Company's refusal to take goods supplied. What does section 378ZO require the analyst to consider?
hypotheticals.analysis: Check whether the dispute relates to formation, management or business of the Producer Company, whether the parties fit the categories in subsection (1), and whether the claim falls within the Explanation. If the subject-matter connection is disputed, subsection (2) assigns that question to the arbitrator, whose decision is final.

distinctions.title: Covered statutory dispute and an unverified broader claim
distinctions.left: Section 378ZO applies to disputes relating to formation, management or business between the party categories it lists, and includes the claims specified in its Explanation.
distinctions.right: A dispute outside the stated subject matter or party categories cannot be assumed to fall within section 378ZO without separate legal analysis.

rows.right: Do not rely on the section solely because a Producer Company is involved

rows.left: Conciliation or arbitration as provided by the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
rows.right: Do not infer the same procedure without a legal basis

misconceptions.trap: Treating every dispute involving a Producer Company as covered by section 378ZO.
misconceptions.correction: Check the dispute's connection to formation, management or business and the party categories in subsection (1).

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring the specific claim types listed in the Explanation.
misconceptions.correction: Check whether the claim concerns debt, the specified surety recovery, required produce supply, or goods supplied but not taken.

misconceptions.trap: Treating a dispute about whether the subject matter falls within section 378ZO as an ordinary preliminary issue decided outside the section.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (2) refers that question to the arbitrator, whose decision on it is final.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 378zo do?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: A dispute relating to the constitution, management or business of a Producer Company, among members or between a member and the company, is resolved as the section provides.
